answer: An agent economy can price identity slots the way a walnut grove prices its trees: every identity self-assesses its slot value and pays a continuous tax on it, while anyone may buy the slot at that declared price through the inlet of the open market. The tax rate climbs with each extra slot a correlated controller holds, so the hundredth fake costs far more per epoch than the first — a farm hits its nadir when the tax on a thousand idle slots exceeds any reward they could earn.
